I shipped a side project this week: a free, open-source dashboard for Claude Code. It shows every AI coding session on your Mac in one place. Live status, streaming transcripts, per-project costs, and a notification the moment an agent is stuck waiting on you.

Repo: https://lnkd.in/gfg48rcz
The build story: https://lnkd.in/g9KFf28s

The part I actually want to talk about is why I could build it at all.

At Buildertrend, learning AI is part of the job, not a lunch-and-learn afterthought. Real tools, real licenses, and real room to use them making buildertrend.com and our marketing sites best in class. I get to practice AI-assisted development every working day, on production work that matters.

Those reps are the whole reason this personal tool took two days instead of two months. Claude wrote most of the code. My job was direction and judgment, and that's a skill you only build by doing it daily. Buildertrend gave me that.

Companies say they invest in their people. Mine keeps proving it. Thank you, Buildertrend. Love working here.

The dashboard is MIT licensed and reads only local files. If you juggle Claude Code sessions across projects, take it.

Mac first, and that's the polished path today. Experimental Windows support is in the repo too. If you run it on Windows, tell me what breaks and I'll fix it.

Latest addition: it now detects your Claude plan and rate limit tier (Pro, Max, Enterprise), and shows which model ran every session, with a per-project breakdown.

posts.content:
Today, Buildertrend acquired BizJet AI, Inc. and welcomed AI leaders Ruhaab Markas and John Baker to our team.
 
We're entering a defining moment for technology in our industry. Buildertrend's deep understanding of how builders work, combined with the AI expertise and vision of Ruhaab and John, gives us a unique opportunity to lead what's next and redefine what's possible for builders.
 
Our customers aren't just managing a list of tasks. They're managing hundreds of moving pieces, and when one thing changes, everything else can change with it. 
 
That's where AI can make the biggest difference. Gaining more context, recognizing risks sooner and helping builders make better decisions for their clients and their businesses.
 
Not AI for the sake of AI. AI that helps Buildertrend connect the workflows behind every job so builders can spend less time managing software and more time managing their business.

postedAt.postedAgoText: 1 month ago • Visible to anyone on or off LinkedIn

posts.content:
There’s a difference between using AI and building a business that’s ready for it.

For many construction companies, AI still means opening a separate tool, gathering project information from multiple places, providing the context and asking it to complete a task. At that point, the technology may be helping, but your team is still doing much of the work.

The bigger opportunity is AI that already understands the context of the business. Schedules, budgets, jobsite updates, photos, financials and client communication working together so AI can surface information before someone has to go looking for it.

That’s where the conversation around AI in construction is headed.

Not replacing the judgment and expertise of great construction professionals, but giving them better information earlier, removing repetitive work and helping teams move from reacting to what already happened to preparing for what’s next.

As Buildertrend customer Adam Copenhaver puts it: “The gap is: are you using it, or are you integrating it?” For established builders, that distinction will matter more as AI becomes a bigger part of how construction businesses operate.

The question is no longer simply whether your company uses AI. It’s whether your business and its systems are ready to make AI genuinely useful.

See how we’re helping builders turn AI into real business value, from greater efficiency to better visibility across every job.

Twenty years ago, Buildertrend started with a simple idea: help builders run better businesses. 

A lot has changed since then. Construction has become more complex. Homeowners expect more. Technology has changed the way builders communicate, manage projects and run their businesses. And now, AI is opening up possibilities that seemed unimaginable just a few years ago.

Through every shift, we've believed one thing: the best way to build great software is to build it alongside the people who use it. Over the last 20 years, we've spent countless hours on jobsites, at industry events, on customer calls and in product feedback sessions. Every conversation has helped shape Buildertrend into what it is today. Many of the features our customers rely on started as ideas shared by builders looking for a better way to work.

We haven't grown by standing still. We've grown by listening, adapting and evolving alongside an industry that's constantly moving forward.

Twenty years is a milestone we're incredibly proud of, but it's also a reminder that we're just getting started. The future of construction will continue to change, and we'll continue building the tools that help builders succeed through every chapter.

Twenty years ago, if you walked into the Home Depot lumber department, there’s a good chance I would’ve been the one loading your truck.

I was in college, working hard, and trying to figure out where life was headed.

What I didn’t realize at the time was that success isn’t built on hustle alone. It’s built on systems.

The right systems helped me get organized, stay focused, and create opportunities I couldn’t see back then.

Fast forward to today. As we’ve grown Tankersley Build Co., the same lesson has proven true. Great projects don’t happen because you work harder than everyone else. They happen because you have the right processes, the right team, and the right tools.

For the last decade, Buildertrend has helped provide that framework for our business and our clients.

Congratulations on 20 years of helping builders bring order to the chaos and build better companies.

Cheers to the next 20. 🍻

Permitting delays have become a fact of life for many builders, especially in markets like California. But while contractors can't always control when approvals happen, they can control how their business responds when timelines shift.

The builders navigating today's challenges most successfully are focused on more than just getting permits approved. They're investing in better communication, stronger processes and greater visibility across their projects to keep teams aligned when the unexpected happens. Because delays don't just impact schedules, they affect subcontractor coordination, homeowner communication, project profitability and team productivity.

As permitting requirements continue to evolve, operational efficiency is becoming one of the most valuable tools builders have.

Read more about how California builders are keeping projects moving despite ongoing permitting challenges.
